correctness.rationale: Affine reduction and the exact Cartesian-product difference body supply a necessary and sufficient antipodality test. Classical rotating support gives n+p planar pairs, including degeneracies. The disjoint classification of horizontal/horizontal, vertical/vertical, horizontal/vertical edge midpoint pairs yields \(n^2+3n+7p\) and independently verifies the vertex count \(n^2+2n+2p\). The resulting defect is algebraic. Standalone exact-integer boundary enumeration passes 187 polygons and is supplementary, not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The simultaneous exact graph-edge and square-cell counts for the antipodal square complex of every affine polygonal prism are a complete, geometrically natural infinite-family classification. Opposite-parallel side pairs have a sharp, fixed five-unit topological defect increment; the counts give useful benchmarks and resolve nontrivial degeneracies beyond the previously known cube or pyramid special cases. The existing universal homology theorem is not re-proved.
